family: GTK2 public preview input trace and source-level arrow/trough junction diagnosis

targeted_input_test.scope_limit: Only left-stepper input was isolated; this does not explain prior intermittent R18 delivery and does not repeat the full arrow matrix.

source_analysis.gtk_source: GTK 2.24.33 exact local source; gtk/gtkrange.c SHA-256 ff0173bf6884704a8172033a5a570c46130635cb6435b0419bcd6d84bb6bb6f6
source_analysis.observed_order: GtkRange paints the trough before each stepper. The Pixbuf engine reconstructs the stepper rectangle from slider-width and stepper-size; a matched STEPPER image returns handled, skipping the fallback GTK box/arrow.
source_analysis.current_theme_mapping: The generator writes a complete opaque 15x15 RGBA stepper raster as overlay_file with overlay_stretch=FALSE. This is not a transparent glyph-only overlay.
source_analysis.geometry_mismatch: For horizontal arrows, GTK 2.24.33 reverse_engineer_stepper_box sets the target rectangle to stepper-size × slider-width = 15×11; for vertical arrows it is 11×15. theme_pixbuf_render with stretch=FALSE centers the 15×15 source without scaling, so the 15×11 target clips two source rows at top and bottom, and the 11×15 target clips two source columns at left and right. This predicts an 11-pixel missing edge strip in the full-cell 15x15 comparison, consistent with the R14 residual.
source_analysis.confidence: Source-level geometric cause is directly supported by GTK and Pixbuf renderer code and the generated 15x15 fully opaque PNG. It strongly explains the R14 seam but still needs an orientation-specific render comparison.
source_analysis.next_discriminating_test: In a disposable private preview, generate orientation-specific full-cell rasters sized 15x11 for horizontal steppers and 11x15 for vertical steppers. Preserve the 11x11 glyph pixels by cropping only the two outer frame rows/columns that GTK necessarily clips; keep relief colors derived from current KDE roles. Compare all four 15x15 reference ROIs and normal/held/released states. Reject if glyph pixels, role-derived colors, or press/release behavior regress.
